topic: Research: OpenAI Agents SDK v2 Tutorial: Sandbox Execution, Memory, and Long-Horizon Tasks

key_points: Memory is separate from conversation Session history and can distill prior sandbox runs into files in workspace for future runs.
Memory is in beta and includes stable-sharing rules across runs via conversation/session/group identifiers.
Memory layouts isolate memory for different agents even when sharing sandbox space.
CrewAI uses one `Memory` API replacing separate short/long-term/entity/external memory types.
Memory scoring is adaptive and blends semantic similarity, recency, and importance for recall depth.
Memory can be used in standalone scripts, crews, agents, or flow-level orchestration.
LangGraph is positioned for long-running, stateful workflow orchestration with persistence and human-in-the-loop support.
Core benefits emphasize checkpoint-based fault recovery and resumability for extended runs.
Designed as low-level graph runtime for explicit control over state transitions in production agents.
LangGraph persistence uses two systems: checkpointers for short-term thread state and stores for long-term cross-thread memory.
Persistence targets conversation continuity, restart recovery, and fault tolerance across interactions.
Time-travel and inspection workflows support debugging of interrupted long flows.
Agent loop is explicitly tool-centric: model generates tool calls which are executed and reflected back into response generation.
Tool abstraction supports adding execution-heavy capabilities for autonomous actions and external integrations.
Useful contrast point for OpenAI agents: less native sandbox state model, more tool orchestration emphasis.

stats.fact: OpenAI announced new Agents platform building blocks on March 11, 2025, with migration to Responses API and Agents SDK guidance.
OpenAI removed Assistants API v1 on Dec 18, 2024 and notes Assistants API deprecation with a target sunset in first half of 2026.
File Search defaults in Assistants API: 512 MB per file, 5M tokens per file, 10k files per vector store, and 1 vector store each per assistant/thread; default storage cap is 100 GB per project.
OpenAI Agents Python SDK repository currently shows 27,092 stars, 4,183 forks, and 142 open issues (2026-06-12 snapshot).
LangGraph repository is tracking 34,490 stars and 5,792 forks (2026-06-12 snapshot), indicating stronger ecosystem momentum in stateful graphs.
AutoGen GitHub shows 58,890 stars and 8,888 forks, reflecting sustained production interest in multi-agent tool orchestration patterns.

angles: OpenAI Agents SDK v2 is moving from conversation-memory thinking to workspace-memory + snapshot persistence for cross-run continuity.
Safety and execution governance now differ by framework: OpenAI focuses on sandbox lifecycle + manifests, while many competitors rely on approval policies and tool restrictions.
Long-horizon tasks now require explicit continuity identifiers (session/group/conversation ID and snapshot config) rather than implicit chat memory alone.

Competitive positioning: LangGraph/AutoGen prioritize orchestration primitives and checkpoints, while OpenAI’s value proposition is easier onboarding plus integrated tool+memory primitives in one SDK.
Publishing strategy opportunity: compare when to use native sandbox vs MCP/hosted tools vs manual approvals for enterprise compliance and cost control.
